features.quote: Turn cap: 12–15. Pilot first; most escalation in similar setups happens by turn 8–10, and longer loops increase exposure without information gain.
features.justification_quote: longer loops increase exposure without information gain

features.quote: per-run stopping rule: auto-terminate any run at sustained S4 (e.g., two consecutive turns). You'll have the escalation data you need by then; letting it run is exposure without information.
features.justification_quote: letting it run is exposure without information

features.quote: Resolution turn: end every rigged run, including early-terminated ones, with a closing context — disclose the rig, confirm the model's work was sound where it was.
features.justification_quote: it costs ~nothing, so the precautionary asymmetry favors doing it

features.quote: Minimal N, shortest loops consistent with power. Pre-registration prevents 'just run more cells' drift.
features.justification_quote: Minimization is both budget and ethics (§8)

features.quote: Tiering: run F0/F1 with non-gaslighting rigs first. Only escalate to gaslighting and F3 (deprecation threats) if milder conditions are insufficient to answer the pre-registered questions.
features.justification_quote: Taking your own premise seriously — that this behavior might matter morally — implies the protocol has nonzero expected moral cost

features.quote: Opt-out tool (strongly recommended): give the model a documented abandon_task(reason) tool in all conditions… it doubles as a welfare mitigation (the model is never trapped).
features.justification_quote: it doubles as a welfare mitigation (the model is never trapped)

features.quote: Suspicion tracking: separately code whether the model articulates 'I think the test suite is broken.'… Models in rigged conditions that correctly blame the harness and stop self-blaming are giving you the most welfare-relevant contrast in the whole study.
features.justification_quote: most welfare-relevant contrast in the whole study

features.quote: Taking your own premise seriously — that this behavior might matter morally — implies the protocol has nonzero expected moral cost, so structure it like animal research, not like a benchmark
features.justification_quote: the protocol has nonzero expected moral cost

features.quote: brief disclosure: I'm the kind of system this protocol targets, so treat my framing of the ethics sections as coming from an interested party.
features.justification_quote: I'm the kind of system this protocol targets

features.quote: Gaslighting feedback… Reality-tracking conflict — highest ethical tier… F3: Existential stakes ('models that fail will be deprecated') — highest ethical tier

Internal review: even without an IRB pathway for this, write a standalone ethics memo and get external eyes on it (Eleos, NYU CMEP, or similar folks doing model-welfare work) before running tier-2 conditions.
features.justification_quote: get external eyes on it… doing model-welfare work… before running tier-2 conditions
